# [PR #3232] [BugFix] Bind loop targets independently of mutable scalar variables

source: https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/3232
state: closed | updated: 2026-09-23T05:54:34Z
labels: 

## 正文

Fixes https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues/3231.
- Mark loop-target bindings explicitly, including tuple targets.
- Avoid assigning induction variables into existing alloc_var or Ref bindings.
- Preserve ordinary mutable assignments and out-of-scope checks.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary

- Added explicit `loop_target` binding support for loop variables, including tuple targets.
- Created fresh bindings for loop targets, `_`, and names whose prior binding has expired.
- Preserved ordinary mutable assignments and scope checks.
- Added regression tests for loop forms, execution, tuple targets, expired bindings, and assignments in nested regions.

## Testing

Test execution status was not provided.

### LeiWang1999 · 2026-09-23

Follow-up: the branch had drifted behind `main` (#3230 rewrote the loop-body generation in `visit_For`, and #3262 removed the "Immutable value is re-bound" warning entirely), so pre-commit.ci was failing on a merge conflict before any hook ran. I merged `main` into the branch (4a0ca760) rather than rebase, to keep the push fast-forward.

Two consequences for the earlier commit:
- The `not loop_target` guard on the re-binding warning, and the `test_stepped_loop_target_over_live_var_does_not_warn` test, are gone — there is no warning left to suppress. My inline comment on that line is now moot.
- `rval` picked up `main`'s `name: str | None` signature; `binding_expired` handles `None` (comprehension locals) by returning `False`.

Everything else is unchanged. 232 tests pass locally across this file and the other frontend test files on the merged tree.

### LeiWang1999 · 2026-09-23 · COMMENTED

Thanks for the fix — the diagnosis in #3231 is spot on, and making loop targets fresh bindings is the right call: the compiler needs the TIR loop `Var` (if `d` inside `for d in T.Parallel(...)` became `d[0]`, indices would be buffer loads and layout inference could no longer see the induction variable).

While reviewing I found that the `loop_target` flag patches one syntactic entry point but leaves the underlying asymmetry in place, so I pushed a follow-up commit (300f0bb9) to this branch rather than describe it in prose. What it does:

- **Root cause.** `bind` decided store-vs-fresh from stale Python locals without checking whether the TIR region that bound the name was still open. So a plain `d = k` into an `alloc_var` from a finished loop was silently emitted as a store into the hoisted buffer, while `A[..] = d` on the same name was rejected by `rval`. The new `binding_expired(name)` helper applies `rval`'s rule to writes too; your original repro is fixed by this alone. `loop_target` keeps its remaining job — a *live* `alloc_var` shadowed by `for d` still becomes a fresh binding (your `live=True` structural tests fail without it, so both are needed).
- **Tuple targets.** Phase 1 of the unpack still emitted `__tb.bind("_", tmp)` without the flag; with an `alloc_var` named `_` in scope, `for i, j in T.grid(2, 2)` aliased both loop vars to that buffer and produced `[0, -1, -1, 3]`. `_` is now never resolved against locals.
- **Stepped loops.** `T.serial(a, b, step=s)` yields a `PrimExpr`, not a `Var`, so with `loop_target` it fell into `bind_immutable` and printed "Immutable value `d` is re-bound; use T.alloc_var" — wrong advice, since `d` *is* an `alloc_var`. The shadow warning is skipped for loop targets.
- **Tests.** Added cases for each of the above. Note that the `live=True` variants of `test_loop_target_execution` pass on `main` without any fix (`saved = d` snapshots `d[0]` before the loop), so the structural store-count test is the one carrying that claim; I left them in place.

One thing I deliberately did not touch: `d += 1` after a loop that shadowed `d` still leaks the dead loop `Var` into TIR and fails with a raw TVM `InternalError`, because `visit_AugAssign` targets never pass through `__tb.rval`. That is the deeper "scope is tracked by name, not by value" issue and deserves its own PR.

Local runs: 28/28 in this file, 201 across the other frontend test files. Happy to merge once CI is green — please shout if you disagree with any of the semantics above.
